headline: Every brand grew; earnings rise and full-year outlook held
summary_short: Williams-Sonoma's Q3 net revenue grew 5.8% on a 5.1% comp, with non-GAAP diluted EPS of $2.19, up 11.7%, and non-GAAP operating margin of 17.4%. Full-year 2026 guidance was reiterated.
summary_long: Every brand and channel posted a positive comp. GAAP gross margin of 47.6% (+150bp) included +140bp from IEEPA tariff refunds; non-GAAP gross margin was 46.2% (+10bp) as occupancy leverage and merchandise margin offset higher oil-driven supply chain costs. SG&A leverage of 30bp helped. Cash was $992M, operating cash flow $279M, and $253M was returned via buybacks and dividends. FY26 outlook: revenue +4.7% to +7.2%, non-GAAP operating margin 17.8%-18.2%.
confidence_notes: GAAP results include IEEPA tariff refunds (a $29.3M reduction of cost of goods sold) that the company excludes from non-GAAP; the non-GAAP figures are the cleaner comparison. Gross margin driver bps are quoted from the release's own attribution.

drivers.explanation: Occupancy leverage of +40bp and higher merchandise margins of +20bp were partly offset by -50bp from higher oil-driven supply chain costs.
SG&A rate fell 30bp on a non-GAAP basis due to employment expense leverage.
Management credits design advantages and the direct sourcing model, allowing more full-price selling; every brand and channel delivered a positive comp.
